web.title: Varmala Ki Unchai: Kitty Party Game Rules, How to Play and Twists
web.description: Varmala Ki Unchai is a funny shaadi theme kitty party game with a dupatta garland and a toffee bribe. Learn what you need, the steps, rules and twists.
web.intro: Varmala Ki Unchai is a shaadi theme kitty party game where one lady plays the dulha and leans back, chin up, to dodge the varmala, while the dulhan has 30 seconds to get a dupatta garland over her head. The dulhan's team scores a point every time the garland lands, and the team with the most varmalas at the end wins. The crazy twist: the dulhan's saheli can bribe the dulha's dost with a toffee, and a dost who takes it must let go of the dulha's elbow. It needs only a dupatta, a few toffees and a phone timer, so it is perfect for wedding season kitties.
materials: One dupatta tied into a loose loop as the varmala
A phone timer set to 30 seconds
steps: Split the room into two teams, Ladkewale and Ladkiwale. Each round, Ladkewale send a dulha and two dost, and Ladkiwale send a dulhan and one saheli.
The dulha stands with her hands behind her back and her feet planted. The two dost stand on either side and hold her elbows, so she can lean back a little and lift her chin.
Start the 30 second timer. The dulhan tries to put the dupatta garland over the dulha's head. She may rise on her toes but cannot jump or stand on anything.
At any time the saheli can offer a toffee to one dost. If the dost takes it she says "Bik gayi!", slowly lets go of the elbow and steps aside, and the dulha must stand straight.
If the garland goes over the head and rests on the shoulders before the timer ends, Ladkiwale get a point. Then swap roles and play again until every lady has had a turn.
rules: If the dulha moves her feet, the varmala counts.
If the dulhan jumps or uses a chair or stool, the point is cancelled.
A dost who takes the toffee but keeps holding gives a point to Ladkiwale.
The garland must rest on the shoulders within 30 seconds to score.
The team with the most varmalas after everyone has played wins.
variations: Pick the tallest lady in the room as the dulha for a near impossible round.
Mummy ji rule: no toffees allowed, the saheli can only bribe the dost with compliments.
The dulhan must recite a one line shaayari after the garland lands before the point counts.
tips: The dulha should lean back only a little; this is about dodging, not falling.
Dost should hold the elbows firmly and let go slowly when bribed.
Play on a carpet or rug and keep furniture and glass tables away.
Use a soft cotton dupatta, not one with heavy zari or pins.

faq.q: How many players do you need for Varmala Ki Unchai?
faq.a: Five ladies play each round: a dulha, two dost, a dulhan and a saheli. With 8 to 20 ladies in two teams, everyone gets a turn in 10 to 15 minutes.

faq.q: What do you need to play Varmala Ki Unchai?
faq.a: Just a dupatta tied into a loop for the varmala, two toffees per round and a phone timer. No shopping needed.

faq.q: Is Varmala Ki Unchai a good game for a shaadi theme kitty party?
faq.a: Yes. It recreates the funny varmala moment from Indian weddings, so it fits shaadi season, sangeet and bridal theme kitties perfectly.

faq.q: Is the game safe for older ladies?
faq.a: Yes, if the dulha only leans back slightly, the dost hold her elbows firmly, and nobody jumps or stands on furniture. Older ladies can happily play dost or saheli.

faq.q: How do you win Varmala Ki Unchai?
faq.a: The dulhan's team scores a point each time the garland lands within 30 seconds. After everyone has had a turn, the team with the most points wins.
